text: The LORD said to Moses:
Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When a man or a woman makes a special vow, the vow of a Nazirite, to set themselves apart for the LORD,
they must abstain from wine and strong drink. They must not drink vinegar made from wine or from strong drink, nor drink any juice of grapes, nor eat grapes, fresh or dried.
As long as they are set apart, they must eat nothing that comes from the grapevine, not even the seeds or the skins.

As long as their vow of separation lasts, no razor may touch their head. Until the time is complete for which they set themselves apart to the LORD, they are holy; they must let the hair of their head grow long.
As long as they are set apart for the LORD, they must not go near a dead body.
Even for their father or mother, brother or sister, they must not make themselves unclean when these die, because the sign of their separation to God is upon their head.
Throughout the days of their separation they are holy to the LORD.
If someone dies suddenly beside them, defiling their consecrated head, they must shave their head on the day of their cleansing—on the seventh day they shall shave it.
On the eighth day they must bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons to the priest at the entrance to the tent of meeting.

The priest shall offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering, and make atonement for them, because they sinned by being in the presence of the dead. That same day they shall consecrate their head again.

They must dedicate themselves to the LORD for the full term of their separation and bring a year-old male lamb as a guilt offering. The previous days do not count, because their separation was defiled.
This is the law of the Nazirite: When the time of their separation is complete, the Nazirite shall be brought to the entrance of the tent of meeting.

versions.text: This is the law of the Nazirite: When the time of their separation is complete, they shall be brought to the entrance of the tent of meeting.
versions.explanation: With the plural 'they' used throughout for the singular Nazirite, 'they shall be brought' can be misheard as referring to the offerings or to other people. Naming the Nazirite keeps the oral reading clear.

text: There they shall present their offering to the LORD: one year-old male lamb without defect for a burnt offering, one year-old ewe lamb without defect for a sin offering, one ram without defect for a fellowship offering,
together with a basket of unleavened bread—loaves of fine flour mixed with oil and unleavened wafers spread with oil—along with their grain offerings and drink offerings.

versions.text: together with a basket of unleavened bread—loaves of fine flour mixed with oil and wafers spread with oil—along with their grain offerings and drink offerings.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew specifies 'wafers of unleavened bread' (רקיקי מצות); adding 'unleavened' before 'wafers' preserves the parallel emphasis of the verse without lengthening it unduly.

text: The priest shall present them before the LORD and make the sin offering and the burnt offering.
He shall offer the ram as a fellowship offering to the LORD, together with the basket of unleavened bread, and shall also make the grain offering and the drink offering.
Then at the entrance to the tent of meeting the Nazirite shall shave their consecrated head, take the hair, and put it on the fire that is under the fellowship offering.

After the Nazirite has shaved off the hair of their consecration, the priest shall take the boiled shoulder of the ram, one loaf of unleavened bread from the basket, and one unleavened wafer, and place them in the hands of the Nazirite.

The priest shall then wave them as a wave offering before the LORD. They are holy and belong to the priest, together with the breast that was waved and the thigh that was presented. After that, the Nazirite may drink wine.

This is the law of the Nazirite who makes a vow: their offering to the LORD for their separation, besides whatever else they can afford. They must do exactly as they vowed, according to the law of their separation.

versions.text: This is the law of the Nazirite who vows an offering to the LORD in keeping with their separation, apart from whatever else they can afford. They must do exactly as they vowed, according to the law of their separation.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has two distinct clauses: 'who makes a vow' and then 'his offering to the LORD for his separation.' The current wording fuses them into 'vows an offering,' which slightly shifts the sense—the vow is the Nazirite vow itself, and the offering is what it requires.

text: The LORD said to Moses:
Tell Aaron and his sons: This is how you are to bless the Israelites. Say to them:
The LORD bless you and keep you;
the LORD make his face shine on you and be gracious to you;
the LORD look upon you with favor and give you peace.
So they will put my name on the Israelites, and I will bless them.
